title: Barcode QC: real counts, threshold trade-offs and saved plots
description: Inspect the published count-table example, run Barcode QC, compare read depth and threshold trade-offs, and open its verified saved plots in a real image viewer.
objectives: Find Barcode QC inside Map Barcodes and choose a real mapped-count table.
Distinguish an illustrative target from an experimentally justified setting.
Inspect console warnings, actual saved plots and independently checked tables.
Separate low-read wells, over-target wells and barcode-sequence collisions.
prerequisite: Use plate_1_unique_combinations.csv from the downloaded example-screen data shown in the Regression tutorial. The source is an existing published count table, NOT output from this tutorial session's unsuccessful raw FASTQ mapping attempt. Its manifest specifies 4325565 bytes and SHA256 9bbfd6de409ec501b94abd2f20230611a695b142228892f5c3b8b2b564ba1f13. Use a private copy and a new output directory. Barcode QC is nested inside Map Barcodes. This real run has 172756 input rows, 49464341 mapped reads in the table, 384 wells and 1379 observed guides. Target 5 with median is demonstration only; other settings are min_reads_per_well=0, starved_read_fraction=0.1, exclude_starved_wells=True, position_effect_ratio=2, sweep_span=4, sweep_points=25, Plot/Save/Verbose on. Optional qc_data and guide/row/column reference files are omitted. Therefore no unmapped-rate, missing-reference-guide or barcode-sequence-collision conclusion is supported. The worker succeeds and independent CSV comparisons check 2884 fields with zero numeric error; original inputs and saved outputs stay unchanged. This build still emits an incorrect src preflight error despite accepting count_data, and its Figures card stays empty. We explicitly show both saved PNGs in the real external system viewer, NOT repaired GUI plotting. There is no live preview control or GPU calculation here. No AI provider is contacted. API: spacr.sequencing_qc.barcode_qc, derive_threshold and threshold_sweep. No biological validation or publication is claimed.

scenes.narration: Open Map Barcodes, then its nested Barcode QC tool. This workflow examines counts after mapping; it does not remap FASTQ reads. We use the published count-table example from the linked Regression lesson. It is not output from our earlier unsuccessful raw-read mapping attempt.

Under Count data, select a copy of plate one unique combinations. Check the selected file rather than leaving a placeholder path. This actual table contains about forty-nine point five million mapped reads across three hundred eighty-four wells. Keep the original unchanged and choose a new destination for the QC outputs.

Target gRNAs per well expresses the target used to derive a read-abundance cutoff. Here we leave the illustrative value five and use the median. That is not a recommended experimental design or proof of single-guide attribution. Choose your own target from the design and inspect the resulting trade-offs, not just the suggested number.

The starved-read fraction identifies wells with unusually few reads relative to the plate median. Here it is zero point one, and none of the three hundred eighty-four wells fall below the resulting cutoff. This is a read-depth flag, not a guarantee that every well, guide or biological measurement is trustworthy.

Enable Plot and Save, keep the destination explicit, and press Run. This is a small table analysis, not a GPU segmentation task, and this screen has no live-preview control. We leave the optional mapping-QC and barcode-reference inputs empty; conclusions requiring those files cannot be inferred from the count table alone.

Read the actual console, including its warnings. The worker finishes, but this build incorrectly complains that src is missing even though the module uses Count data. We verified the real input and saved tables; we did not repair the preflight. Do not generalize this diagnosed mismatch into permission to ignore other errors.

The current build also leaves its Figures panel empty although two PNG plots were saved. Open barcode underscore qc dot png and threshold underscore sweep dot png from your output folder in an image viewer. The next scenes show the real system viewer, not figures inserted into spaCR or a claim that the GUI is fixed.

Inspect read depth, row and column effects, and the observed library distribution. The dashed depth cutoff identifies low-read wells; the position bars compare row or column medians with the plate median. The library curve shows unequal read representation among observed guides. Without a reference library, it cannot tell you which expected guides are entirely missing.

Inspect the sweep rather than accepting a cutoff blindly. Here the derived threshold is about zero point zero one two one, or one point two one percent of a well's reads. It gives a median of five guides, retains all wells and about fifty-eight percent of mapped reads, while roughly forty percent of wells still exceed the target.

The red curve counts wells over the five-guide target. It is not a measurement of barcode-sequence similarity, and being below that target does not establish single-guide attribution. Loosening the cutoff raises the over-target fraction without gaining wells here. Compare the saved sweep table, and justify a choice for your analysis rather than treating this example as a universal threshold.

Keep the source counts, settings, console log, recommendation, tables and plots together. Independent checks reproduced the saved well, position and sweep statistics with no numerical discrepancy. That verifies this computation, not its biological interpretation. AI assistance is optional and no request was submitted here; any later advice must be checked against the actual data and API.
